name: MODE.SNGL
description: MODE.SNGL returns the most frequently occurring numeric value in a dataset. It is the modern replacement for the legacy MODE function.
tldr: Returns the single most frequent value, choosing the lowest on a tie.

parameters.name: number1
parameters.description: The first number, cell, or range to evaluate.

basicExample.description: Most frequent value in a small list
basicExample.explanation: 2 appears twice, more often than any other value.

advancedExamples.title: Tied frequencies return the smallest mode
advancedExamples.scenario: Two values share the top frequency
advancedExamples.description: MODE.SNGL returns one value and prefers the lowest when tied.
advancedExamples.explanation: Both 2 and 3 occur twice; the smaller value, 2, is returned.

advancedExamples.title: Mode from a range with blanks
advancedExamples.description: Empty cells are ignored when counting frequencies.
advancedExamples.explanation: 5 occurs three times, the highest frequency in the set.

howItWorks: MODE.SNGL counts the frequency of each numeric value and returns the value with the greatest frequency. When several values tie, it returns the smallest of them. If no value repeats it returns #N/A. Text, logical values, and empty cells are ignored. It is identical in behavior to the legacy MODE.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the mode.

limitations: Returns only a single value even when multiple values tie for the highest frequency.
Returns #N/A when all values are unique.
Ignores text labels, so a repeated category name is not counted.

commonErrors.cause: No value repeats in the supplied data.
commonErrors.fix: Use MODE.MULT to return all tied values, or confirm the data has duplicates.

commonErrors.cause: Repeated values are stored as text and ignored.
commonErrors.fix: Convert text entries to numbers before applying MODE.SNGL.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports MODE.SNGL with the same syntax and result as Excel.

faq.question: Is MODE.SNGL the same as MODE?
faq.answer: Yes, they behave identically. MODE.SNGL is the name introduced in Excel 2010; MODE remains for compatibility.

faq.question: How is it different from MODE.MULT?
faq.answer: MODE.MULT can return several values (an array) when multiple modes exist, while MODE.SNGL returns only one.

faq.question: What happens with a tie?
faq.answer: MODE.SNGL returns the smallest value among those tied for the highest frequency.
